title:
Comment of Alison Bennett in Docket(s)/Project(s) P-15423-000
Submission Date: 10/28/2026

documents.name: 151894.txt
documents.text:
Alison Bennett, Potomac, MD.
I object to a data center that will endanger the 331 beluga whales left in the Cook Inlet. This is a 75% decline from their historic population of about 1,300 in 1979. The proposed project would span 1,400-1,650 offshore acres near Nikiski, including up to 350 tidal turbines, 66 subsea data-center pods, and a 3.5-mile underwater sea cable. That's precisely where the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) designates 7,800 sq kilometers as beluga’s ‘critical habitat.’  Belugas are among NOAA’s marine species at greatest near-term extinction risk. Beluga whales are already competing with commercial shipping, port and coastal development, oil and gas exploration and production, and other anthropogenic activities, like fishing. A recent study found that discharges from data centers alter oxygen and acid levels in the water and sediment increasing stresses for these endangered animals. Please reject this project and save the whales.
